mechanism_chains.title: Concentrated fluorinated electrolyte to interphase-controlled lithium efficiency
mechanism_chains.chain_summary: A concentrated LiFSI/FDEE electrolyte supports an anion-rich solvation structure, which promotes a LiF-rich interphase and is associated with high lithium plating/stripping Coulombic efficiency under the reported condition.

findings.statement: The supplied evidence supports that an anion-rich solvation structure promotes formation of a LiF-rich interphase and suppresses parasitic reactions.
findings.scope_boundary: This finding is limited to the reported electrolyte system and does not establish that every route to stronger anion coordination improves fast-charging performance.
uncertainties: Transferability beyond the reported electrolyte chemistry and matched test conditions is not established.

research_leads.title: Test whether anion coordination is a transferable interphase-design variable
research_leads.research_question: Across matched high-voltage lithium-metal electrolyte variants, how does changing anion coordination strength relate to interphase chemistry and fast-charging stability beyond the reported LiFSI/FDEE formulation?
research_leads.investigation_target: Transferability of the anion-rich-solvation to LiF-rich-interphase relationship across controlled electrolyte variants.
research_leads.rationale: The current finding is boundary-limited to the reported concentrated LiFSI/FDEE condition, while the mechanism chain identifies anion-rich solvation and LiF-rich interphase formation as linked steps. This creates a well-grounded transferability question without establishing what direction an alternative formulation will produce.
boundary_conditions: matched electrolyte variants with controlled confounders
research_leads.scientific_significance: Determining transferability would show whether anion coordination is a reusable research variable rather than a property specific to one reported formulation.
uncertainties: The supplied packet does not establish transferability across electrolyte families.
The relative contribution of salt concentration, fluorinated solvent chemistry, and anion coordination is not isolated.

focus_questions: Turn the accepted transferability lead into a bounded, falsifiable hypothesis without presenting it as established.
